summary_html: Agency places a child with **relatives or kin caregivers** instead of non-relative foster care. Federal law favors kinship care as least-restrictive, family-preserving placement.
authority_html:
- **Fostering Connections to Success and Increasing Adoptions Act (FCSIAA 2008)** — kinship-care incentives  
- **SSA Title IV-E (42 U.S.C. §§ 670–679c)** — reimbursement for approved kin placements

primary_citations.citation_text: Maryland - Md. Code, Family Law Article §§ 5-701 et seq. (Child Abuse and Neglect; definitions at § 5-701, mandatory reporting at §§ 5-704 and 5-705, investigation at § 5-706, appeal of findings at § 5-706.1)
Maryland - Courts & Judicial Proc. § 3-801 et seq. (CINA—Child in Need of Assistance proceedings)

provisions_triggered.name: Due Process / Law of the Land

case_law.method: v1.1.0 case-law rebuild: authorities selected per decision point, each opinion retrieved from CourtListener and read; holding and quote taken from the opinion text; independently re-verified before release. Previous keyword-matched Justia listings were removed.

key_cases.court: Court of Special Appeals of Maryland
key_cases.holding: The court vacated orders removing reunification from the permanency plan because the juvenile court relied on a polygraph examination, holding that material the department may lawfully use as an investigative tool is not thereby admissible as evidence in an adjudicative proceeding.
key_cases.relevance: The children were placed with a paternal grandmother rather than in stranger foster care.
key_cases.quote: we must maintain the careful distinction between an investigative tool and evidence that has sufficient reliability for consideration in an adjudicative proceeding

key_cases.case_name: In re Adoption of Jayden G.
key_cases.holding: The Court affirmed termination, holding that whether to stay a TPR case while an appeal of a permanency-plan change is pending is committed to the juvenile court's discretion and that the court properly considered the child's attachment to his foster parents.
key_cases.relevance: The opinion addresses the department's exploration of a grandmother as a relative resource before the plan changed to non-relative adoption.
key_cases.quote: whether to stay a TPR case is within the juvenile court's discretion

key_cases.citation: No. 1609, Sept. Term 2024 (Md. App. Ct. July 1, 2025)
key_cases.holding: The court held that in CINA cases a department is generally required under the ADA to make reasonable accommodations for parents with disabilities in providing reunification services, provided the parent makes the disability and needed accommodation known, and affirmed the award of custody and guardianship to the grandparents.
key_cases.relevance: It approves kinship permanency with grandparents coupled with supervised parental visitation.
key_cases.quote: the Department is generally required under the ADA to make reasonable accommodations for parents with disabilities in rendering reunification efforts in CINA cases

key_cases.holding: The Court held that a sibling seeking visitation over a parent's objection is a third party who must make the Koshko threshold showing of parental unfitness or exceptional circumstances, and it remanded for consideration of jurisdiction and of deleterious effect on the siblings.
key_cases.relevance: It controls when a juvenile court may order contact between a child in care and kin or siblings living with a parent.
key_cases.quote: A person, thus, seeking visitation, who is not a biological or adoptive parent is a third party. A sibling, whether full, half or CINA, remains a third party.

key_cases.holding: The Court reversed a grandparent-visitation order and overruled contrary prior decisions, holding that Maryland's grandparent visitation statute may be applied constitutionally only after a threshold finding of parental unfitness or exceptional circumstances showing current or future detriment to the child from the absence of visitation, before any best-interest analysis.
key_cases.relevance: It is the source of the threshold showing a relative or other third party must make before a court may order contact with a child over a parent's objection.
key_cases.quote: there must be a finding of either parental unfitness or exceptional circumstances demonstrating the current or future detriment to the child, absent visitation from his or her grandparents

common_failures: Failure to consider less restrictive alternatives

timeline_requirements.deadline: Not later than the next day on which the circuit court is in session, unless extended on good cause shown
timeline_requirements.starts_from: Local department files the petition to authorize continued shelter care after the child is not returned to the parent, guardian, or custodian
